questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
What is likely to be introduced in the market for bus travel if an economy moved from a mixed economy to a market economy?

options.A: allowing companies to bid for bus routes
options.B: free bus travel for school children

questions.questionText: The diagram shows that the production possibility frontier of maize and beans has changed from PPF to PPF .
An individual buys a ticket to visit a government-owned art gallery. How would this visit be classified by an economist?

options.A: private and demerit good

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a shift in a firm’s supply curve from S to S .

A change in the price of a good causes an increase in the quantity of the good demanded. What would be the nature of the good and the direction of price change for this to be certain to happen? nature of good price change

options.A: inferior fall

questions.questionText: Which combination is most likely to result in the demand for a product being highly price elastic? number of close % of income substitutes spent on product

options.A: large large

questions.questionText: A manufacturer increases the price of his product from $4 in an attempt to increase total revenue. The table shows the outcome of the policy. price total revenue ($) 000’s ($)
A firm establishes that the price elasticity of supply of its product has a value of 0.3. What is likely to be true about the firm?

options.A: It has unused productive capacity.
options.B: It has unsold stock of its product.
options.C: It uses a high proportion of perishable raw materials.
options.D: It uses factors of production that are easily substituted.

questions.questionText: There is a reduction in world oil supplies due to war in some supplying countries at a time when the winter in some importing countries was much colder than usual. The diagram shows the original equilibrium price, P. S price of oil S S P P P P P D D D O quantity of oil What will be the equilibrium price of oil in these circumstances?

options.A: P B P C P D P

questions.questionText: Good X is a substitute for good Y and a complement to good Z. What would happen after a fall in the price of good X?

options.A: Only the demand for X will rise.
options.B: Demand for X, Y and Z will rise.
options.C: Demand for Y will fall and for Z will rise.
options.D: Demand for Y will rise and for Z will fall.

questions.questionText: A government imposes a specific indirect tax on a product. When will the tax cause the greatest reduction in consumer surplus for the buyers of the product?

options.A: The product has price elastic demand and price elastic supply.
options.B: The product has price elastic demand and price inelastic supply.
options.C: The product has price inelastic demand and price elastic supply.
options.D: The product has price inelastic demand and price inelastic supply.

questions.questionText: The table shows the maximum amount three students would each be willing to pay for a taxi to take them home from a nightclub. $ Jane 10.00 Sara 8.00 Yasmin 6.00 Assume they share the taxi fare as shown in the table below. Which shows how much they each should pay so that they each obtain the same consumer surplus? Jane Sara Yasmin $ $ $
A government fixes a minimum price for a service. What will be the outcome of such a policy?

options.A: Demand will fall if the minimum price is below the equilibrium price.
options.B: Demand will rise if the minimum price is above the equilibrium price.
options.C: Production will fall if the minimum price is above the equilibrium price.
options.D: Production will stay the same if the minimum price is below the equilibrium price.

questions.questionText: The diagram illustrates the effects of placing a specific tax equal to JM on a good. S price S J X L K Y Z M D O quantity Which area represents total tax receipts?

options.A: JKM B XJKY C XJLY D XJMZ

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand curve, D , and the supply curve, S , for a good.

Planned government expenditure for the UK in the fiscal year 2016 is estimated at £760 billion. The top five areas of expenditure are given in the table. £ billion pensions 153 healthcare 138 welfare 111 education 89 defence 45 total top five 536 What is the total amount spent on transfer payments shown in the table?

options.A: £89 billion B £111 billion C £264 billion D £536 billion

questions.questionText: What is likely to occur when the government privatises public sector monopolies?

options.A: Consumer choice will increase.
options.B: Employment will increase in the short run.
options.D: The production of public goods will increase.

questions.questionText: In a closed economy a rise in aggregate demand is needed to increase output in the country. What is necessary to achieve this increase in output in the economy?

options.A: enough capacity to produce the extra goods and services demanded
options.B: free trade to allow imports to make up any shortages in supply
options.C: government spending to be less than tax revenue

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the long-run aggregate supply (LRAS) curve of an economy. At which equilibrium level of national income is a balance of trade surplus likely to cause the greatest inflationary increase for the economy? LRAS price level O A B C D real national income
A government succeeds in changing a current account deficit into a current account surplus. Why might this current account surplus increase the country’s inflation rate?

options.A: It raises aggregate demand.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows Greece’s trade position with the EU and Russia between 2005 and 2014. key Greek 50 imports from EU trade 40 exports to EU $bn imports from Russia exports to Russia 2005 2006 2007 2008 2009 2010 2011 2012 2013 2014 What can be concluded about the period 2005 to 2014?

options.A: Greece’s annual trade deficit with the EU rose continuously.
options.B: Greece’s annual trade deficit with the EU was lower in 2014 than in 2005.
options.C: Greece’s annual trade deficit with the EU fell continuously.
options.D: Greece’s annual trade deficit with the EU was smaller than its deficit with Russia.

questions.questionText: There is a rise in the exchange rate of the US$. Which would cause the greatest increase in the US current account deficit?

options.A: a high level of domestic unemployment
options.B: a high price elasticity of demand for imports
options.C: a low price elasticity of demand for exports
options.D: a low rate of domestic inflation

questions.questionText: Since 2000 a country’s export prices have increased on average by 50% and its import prices by 25%. What is the current figure for the country’s terms of trade (2000 = 100)?

Each diagram shows the production possibility curves of two economies, X and Y, which produce food and clothes. In which diagram would both economies benefit by specialising in the good in which they have comparative advantage and trading at an exchange rate of 1 unit of clothes to 1.5 units of food?

options.A: B C D

questions.questionText: Four countries, A, B, C and D, trade internationally. Each circle in the diagram represents a free trade area between the countries within the circle. A country can belong to more than one free trade area. Countries outside of a circle face trade barriers. Which country has the greatest opportunity to benefit from free international trade? A C B D
A small trading country decides on a policy of import substitution by producing for itself. What is the most likely reason for this policy?

options.A: to follow the principle of absolute advantage
options.B: to influence world prices in international markets
options.C: to protect local industries from foreign competition
options.D: to substitute imported machines for local labour

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a government’s revenue and expenditure for three years. revenue expenditure revenue expenditure revenue expenditure 0 1 2 3 4 $m What can be concluded from the diagram?

options.A: A budget deficit was replaced by a budget surplus.
options.C: The economy moved from a recession into a boom period.
options.D: The yield from taxation continuously increased.

questions.questionText: A country with a fixed exchange rate has a current account surplus on its balance of payments. What is most likely to reduce this surplus?

options.A: higher interest rates

questions.questionText: In recent years an economy has experienced changes in its price level as shown. percentage change of price level 2010 2015 –2 Which government policy is most effective in reversing the trend shown in the price level?

options.A: encourage firms to expand production through tax incentives
options.B: introduce an incomes policy to directly control wage increases
options.C: promote household savings by issuing savings bonds
